sources.search_query: Germany official visa exemption list states whose citizens require visa auswaertiges-amt
sources.relevant_excerpt: Overview of visa requirements/exemptions for entry into the Federal Republic of Germany. "Persons who do not require a visa to enter Germany (holders of passports from the countries marked 'no' on the list) may, as a general rule, not remain on German territory for more than 90 days in any 180-days period." Hong Kong/Macao note: "The visa waiver applies to holders of SAR passports (Hong Kong and Macao Special Administrative Region passports)." Taiwan note: exemption "applies only to holders of passports issued by Taiwan which include an identity card number." Georgia note: "Holders of official passports require a visa." Countries marked as NOT requiring a visa include (as listed): Austria, Australia, Belgium, Bulgaria, Croatia, Cyprus, Czech Republic, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Greece, Hungary, Iceland, Ireland, Israel, Italy, Japan, South Korea, Latvia, Lithuania, Luxembourg, Malta, Netherlands, New Zealand, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Singapore, Slovak Republic, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, Taiwan, UAE, UK, USA, Uruguay, Albania, Andorra, Antigua and Barbuda, Argentina, Bahamas, Barbados, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Brazil, Brunei Darussalam, Canada, Chile, Colombia, Costa Rica, Dominica, El Salvador, Georgia, Grenada, Guatemala, Honduras, Kiribati, Kosovo, Liechtenstein, Macao, Mauritius, Mexico, Micronesia, Moldova, Monaco, Montenegro, Nicaragua, North Macedonia, Palau, Panama, Paraguay, Peru, Saint Kitts and Nevis, Saint Lucia, Saint Vincent and the Grenadines, Samoa, San Marino, Serbia, Seychelles, Solomon Islands, Timor-Leste, Tonga, Trinidad and Tobago, Tuvalu, Ukraine, Vatican City, Venezuela. China, India, Russian Federation are marked as requiring a visa.

sources.search_query: Germany foreign ministry tourist visa requirements auswaertiges-amt visa regulations
sources.relevant_excerpt: "Third-country nationals require a visa to enter the Federal Republic of Germany." EU nationals and citizens of countries with abolished visa requirements are exempt for stays up to 90 days. A Schengen visa "entitles the holder to visits of up to 90 days every 6 months in the entire Schengen area." The processing fee is "normally EUR 90" for short-stay visas; reduced rates of EUR 35 apply to nationals of specific countries (e.g. Albania, Armenia, Ukraine). Applications must be submitted to "Embassies and Consulates General (missions abroad) of the Federal Republic of Germany"; some applications can be submitted through the Consular Services Portal at digital.diplo.de for certain visa categories. Applications may also be submitted at the "visa application centre at your place of residence" (external service providers working with German missions).

sources.relevant_excerpt: "On the planned date of departure from Germany, your passport has to be valid at least for another three months and it has to be issued within the last 10 years." The travel document "should also contain at least two empty pages where the visa can be inserted." Visitors may "stay in the entire Schengen area for up to 90 days in any period of 180 days." "Visas have to be applied for prior to entry at the German mission abroad covering the place of residence of the applicant." For private visits an invitation is usually required; applicants may need "proof that you have sufficient funds to maintain yourself during your stay and to finance the return trip."

sources.search_query: site:diplo.de Schengen visa application VFS Global external service provider
sources.relevant_excerpt: FAQ: Outsourcing in the visa section - VFS and the German missions in India. "Following the successful conclusion of a regional tender procedure for Southeast Asia/East Asia conducted in Berlin, the company VFS Global was awarded the service concession for the outsourcing of visa application acceptance." "Appointments for Schengen visa applications are no longer offered at the German missions abroad in India. Applications will only be accepted by our partner VFS Global." "The external service provider charges every applicant as approved by German government between 10,-- and 20,-- EUR to be paid in INR at current exchange rate." Only spouses of EU/German citizens can apply directly at missions for Schengen visas without appointments. The page references VFS Global at https://visa.vfsglobal.com/ind/en/deu/privacy-policy.

European Commission (EU-level authority for the Schengen visa regime that includes Germany): "The European Travel Information and Authorisation System (ETIAS) is currently not in operation and no applications for travel authorisations are collected at this point." The launch date will be announced "several months prior to its launch." ETIAS will target "visa-free travellers visiting 30 European countries for a short stay (i.e. for up to 90 days within any 180-day period)". The fee is EUR 20.
sources.effective_date_evidence: Page states ETIAS is currently not in operation; launch date to be announced several months prior to launch

sources.search_query: germany.info Schengen visa fee 90 euro children germany missions united states
sources.relevant_excerpt: Visa Fees - Federal Foreign Office (German Missions in the United States). Schengen visas (including airport transit): Adults 90 EUR; children 0-5 years free; children 6-11 years 45 EUR; children 12+ years 90 EUR. Citizens of Albania, Armenia, Azerbaijan, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Georgia, North Macedonia, Moldova, Montenegro, Serbia, and Ukraine qualify for "a reduced Schengen visa fee of 35 EUR." National visas: adults 75 EUR, children under 18: 37.50 EUR. "Visa fees can be paid in USD only and therefore may vary depending on the daily exchange rate. The German missions in the U.S. accept cash and credit cards. Checks are not accepted." Fee exemptions include spouses of German/EU nationals, scholarship recipients, researchers with doctorates, and students on educational trips.
